svg.title: Maknae per-turn credential path
svg.desc: UML sequence diagram of one model turn's credential path across the user, the trust plane, the Egress Daemon and Vault.
svg.text: The per-turn credential path — who can see a user's model key
One session.prompt turn, end to end (ADR-0028 decision 5). The client makes a wrapped read with the user's own Vault token and seals the
wrapping token to the Egress Daemon; maknaed decides on metadata and forwards the sealed bytes it cannot open. Each step names its code and its test.
2. load the user token; choose the providers.yaml entry
sees: wrapping token (exchangeable once for the key)
5. seal the wrapping token to seal.pub; AAD = conversation, provider, model, path, field
7. admit (peer-uid username, set, model, subpath, field), PDP, destination stamp: metadata only
sees: metadata, prompt content (#417), sealed blob (opaque)
9. open the seal under this request's AAD
Residual, accepted (#429): any process running as the user can make this read itself and call the provider without maknaed; nothing correlates such reads with turns yet.
Residual (#417): prompt content still transits maknaed, and the AAD does not bind it, so maknaed could pair a sealed token with content of its choosing.
On this path the plaintext key exists only inside the Egress Daemon, for one call: a zeroizing buffer, dropped after the call, with no key cache.
A refusal reaches the user only as "not authorized" (the CLI prints PROMPT_REFUSED); the reason is in the audit trail, for the administrator.
